# Settings portability: round 2 exchange A

Reviewer: Fable 5.1, dialogue only. HEAD 9731cee, 115 JVM tests, 0 failures. Nothing built or run. Only this file written.

## Orchestrator challenge acknowledged

Three corrections to my gate 3, all yours.

- Package name. `ly.com.tahaben.farhan` is the Gradle namespace. The installed package is the applicationId, `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha` (`app/build.gradle.kts:17`). Any shell command must use the applicationId.
- Byte-for-byte `dumpsys` comparison is wrong. Process ids, activity records and timestamps change between launches. Compare only the component-name to raw-override map.
- The owner's phone is the wrong device. The old debuggable install carries the same applicationId as the test build, so installing the androidTest pair there means uninstalling the only old-settings copy. Gate 3 runs on an emulator or a second device, never on the owner's install.

## Reviewer reasoned answer

Yes, one instrumentation case against the real Android adapter satisfies gate 3, provided it has these properties.

1. It constructs `ly.com.tahaben.farhan.settings.RecoveryComponents` with the target context and calls `block()` and `heal()` through it. The JVM tests already cover the protocol; the adapter is the only untested code.
2. Before `block()`, it puts real components into every raw state the protocol branches on: a manifest-enabled component left DEFAULT, one set to explicit ENABLED (the WorkManager shape), one set to explicit DISABLED, and a manifest-disabled component left DEFAULT. The merged manifest has manifest-disabled components at `captures/settings/build-attempt2/evidence/app-manifest.xml:283-313`, so no fixture is needed for that case.
3. It records the map M0 of `getComponentEnabledSetting` over every name from the adapter's `list()`, then asserts after `block()`: return true, marker ENABLED, both manifest-enabled DEFAULT and ENABLED components now DISABLED, the explicit DISABLED and the manifest-disabled components unchanged, and `list()` still returns the same names.
4. It builds a second `RecoveryComponents` instance, calls `heal()`, and asserts the map equals M0 exactly, the marker is DISABLED, and `no_backup/component_states_v1` is gone.
5. Teardown restores M0 whatever the outcome, so a red run does not leave the test install blocked.

The three platform facts this one case settles are the ones no JVM test can. First, `ComponentInfo.enabled` under `GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS` reports the manifest value and not the effective state. Second, `getPackageInfo` with that flag still lists components whose override is DISABLED. This one is the most dangerous and I did not name it in round 2: after `block()` every normal component is override-disabled, and if the listing dropped them, `heal()` would compute an empty name set and restore nothing. Third, `setComponentEnabledSetting(DEFAULT, DONT_KILL_APP)` returns an explicitly ENABLED component to raw 0, and the raw values survive the string round trip in the snapshot file. A fourth fact is cheaper: PackageManager accepts only DEFAULT, ENABLED and DISABLED for components, so `checked()` never throws on a phone. That is from memory of PackageManagerService, and the M0 capture confirms or refutes it for free.

For a shell cross-check on an emulator, read `dumpsys package ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha` and compare only the `enabledComponents:` and `disabledComponents:` sets under the user block. A component in neither set is DEFAULT. That recovers the same map as the test.

Gate 2 stays as the existing `AndroidImportJournalTest` (three cases). Gate 4, the staged real import, runs on the same disposable install. Note that `HiltTestRunner` swaps in a test application, so `FarhanApplication.onCreate` and the startup coordinator do not run under instrumentation. Gate 4 must call the Android `SettingsStartup` entry directly in the test, or launch the debug APK on the emulator with a staged journal and observe Applied by hand. Either is fine. The JVM coordinator tests already cover the acknowledgement path.

Nothing in the adapter depends on Pixel behaviour. The listener rebind and accessibility toggles are pilot evidence, as agreed.

On the dependency: yes. The helper has applicationId `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_rescue` (`settings_rescue/build.gradle.kts:14`), reads the old install over wireless ADB and writes a file. It never imports into the old app, and its invariants (no success for a failed capture, no credentials in the file, no stale bridge reply finishing another export) are pinned by its 56 JVM tests. Sending it as an unverified pilot helper after a clean compile does not claim the main import is ready. The owner's paired export is owner evidence. Its own two instrumented tests remain unrun and the send note should say so.

No score changes. Durability stays at 8. The corrected gate set is: full assemble of both APKs; `AndroidImportJournalTest`; the one adapter case above; the staged import round trip. All four on a disposable install. Pass means 9 and APPROVE with no further code round, as round 2 said.

# Settings portability: review round 2

Reviewer: Fable 5.1, review only (owner approved 5.1 because 5.2 is unavailable). Diff `git diff 3f5eb31 9731cee -- app build.gradle.kts settings_portability settings_rescue`, HEAD 9731cee. Nothing was built or run. The only file written is this one. About 25 minutes.

Read in full: the diff; both new test files; the new `RecoveryComponents.kt` and `SettingsStartup.kt` in settings_portability; app `ProcessStores`, `SettingsStartup`, `RecoveryComponents`, `RecoveryActivity`, `FarhanApplication`, `PrivateSettingsFiles`, `SettingsBackupActivity` around the dialog; `ImportCoordinator` and `ImportJournal` for the startup contract; rescue `RescueActivity` layout helpers, `CaptureEngine` constructor, `AdbBridgeService.withConnection`, cancel path, manifest and strings; root and module Gradle files; round-1 review, argument and fixes reports; the ledger.

Evidence I checked myself, not taken from the reports:

- JUnit XML under `captures/settings/build-attempt2`: portability 59 tests, rescue 56 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. `RecoveryComponentsTest` (7) and `SettingsStartupTest` (7) are in the portability run, so the 14 new tests executed under the real Android Gradle invocation.
- Merged app manifest in `captures/settings/build-attempt2/evidence/app-manifest.xml:177-193`: `LegacySenderService`, `JobSenderService` and `AcraContentProvider` all declare `android:process=":acra"`. The round-1 hardening item is now a confirmed path, not a memory.
- ACRA 5.12.0 `ACRA.kt` (fetched, tag acra-5.12.0): `object ACRA`, `@JvmStatic fun isACRASenderServiceProcess(): Boolean`, public, matches `/proc/self/cmdline` against `":acra"`. The Kotlin call in `FarhanApplication.kt:34` resolves. Not compiled here.
- Merged rescue manifest before the fix listed `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `READ_PHONE_STATE`, `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`. Those three are the manifest merger's implied permissions for a library AAR with no `targetSdkVersion`, not permissions from `:settings_android`. Removing them is correct.
- No code outside `ProcessStores` opens `shared_pref`, `farhan_data_store` or `farhan_db` (grep over app, core, core_ui, notification_filter, settings_android). The gate covers every consumer; `AppModule.kt:45,53,85` are the only providers.
- Build log `boat-build-20261118T075152Z.log`: the root build configured `:settings_portability`, ran its tests, compiled `:settings_rescue`, and failed only at `:app:compileDebugKotlin:91` on the `Button` receiver. That failure is the line fixed in this diff.

## Round-1 findings

- **S1 resolved.** `RecoveryComponentProtocol.heal()` (`settings_portability/.../RecoveryComponents.kt:71-79`) filters the snapshot by `normalComponents()` names before any `set`. `healingSkipsRemovedAndLeavesNewComponentsAlone` pins it, and the Rig's `set` throws for a removed name, so dropping the filter goes red. New components are untouched, and `blockExtendsSnapshotForNewComponents` pins the snapshot extension before the new component's disable.
- **S2 resolved as a code and test finding.** The protocol, gate and coordinator are real production classes; the Android adapter has no branching beyond PackageManager calls and a `toInt` map. I ran the round-1 mutations in my head against the tests: `snapshot.write` after the disable loop fails `snapshotPrecedesDisablesAndRepeatedBlockDoesNothing` on the literal event list; `gate.open()` before `heal()` fails `healRunsWithEveryStoreStillDenied` because heal asserts denial; dropping `snapshot.clear()` fails the `assertNull(saved)` checks; dropping `gate.close()` fails the test that opens the gate first; dropping the catch-path `block()` fails `healFailureKeepsGateClosedAndBlocksComponents`; dropping the `components.get(name) != expected` guard fails on the event list (Hidden and UserDisabled would be written). The crash test walks all eight durable boundaries with a fresh platform built only from durable maps. The instrumented `AndroidImportJournal` test is still unrun; that is the open gate below, as agreed in round 1.
- **S3 resolved.** Intro, export body, SOURCE_CHANGED and after-save text say turn off the old Farhan's notification access before export, keep it closed, and check both permissions afterwards if the old app is kept. Force-stop "may" turn off accessibility; no version range, no rebind claim. The shortcut opens `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SETTINGS` with a plain Settings fallback. The owner can now act on the error. The Pixel 9a device check remains evidence, not a bar item.
- **S4 resolved.** The root build configured `:settings_portability` with the `jetbrainsKotlinJvm apply false` line present (attempt 1 and attempt 2 logs). Whether it would also have configured without the line is unknown and does not matter: the line is the conventional form and the build is observed to configure.

## New findings

None at blocker or should. I looked for an in-scope failure in the new code and did not find one. What follows is a verification gate, not a defect.

The code I read reaches durability 9 only once four facts that no JVM test can establish have been observed. Two of the diff's lines (`FarhanApplication.kt:34`, `SettingsBackupActivity.kt:91`) are uncompiled, the production journal has never round-tripped a record on Android, and the Android component adapter has never executed. The adapter maps two platform behaviours nobody has watched: `ComponentInfo.enabled` for manifest-disabled components under `GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS`, and `setComponentEnabledSetting(..., DEFAULT, DONT_KILL_APP)` restoring WorkManager's explicitly ENABLED proxies. The protocol is correct on paper; the paper has to meet the phone once.

Gates, in the order that gives the most information per minute:

1. Full assemble of 9731cee for both APKs. Resolves the two uncompiled corrections.
2. Instrumented `AndroidImportJournal` test: every phase round-trips, including `previous` with raw values of the "wrong" type.
3. On the Pixel 9a (debuggable build): capture `dumpsys package ly.com.tahaben.farhan` component states; write garbage into `no_backup/settings_import_v1` with `run-as`; launch; confirm every normal component is disabled and the recovery icon appears; delete the garbage; launch; confirm `dumpsys` states equal the capture byte for byte and the recovery icon is gone. This is the one run that proves the adapter.
4. Stage a real export, kill, relaunch, see Applied, acknowledge; then roll back once by making a store fail if that is cheap, otherwise accept the JVM rollback tests.

Gates 1 to 4 passing moves durability to 9 and the verdict to APPROVE with no further code round. The S3 pidof and accessibility check and the real helper pair, export, import run are the pilot's owner evidence (`owner-ok`), not conditions for the bar.

## Scores

SCORE[durability]: 8/10 (every round-1 defect is fixed and pinned by tests that executed; held at 8 until gates 1 to 4 above have run, as round 1 agreed; bar 9)
SCORE[error-paths]: 8/10 (fail-closed paths are pinned on the production classes; SOURCE_CHANGED advice is actionable; stashed nits only; bar 6)
SCORE[security]: 8/10 (no in-model exposure; three implied permissions removed from the helper; the `:acra` process no longer touches the journal; bar 6)
SCORE[architecture]: 8/10 (the port extraction is the right shape and the adapter stayed thin; root build configures; bar 6)
SCORE[legibility]: 8/10 (claims cite the test that proves them; two comment nits below; bar 6)
VERDICT: CHANGES (durability 8 against a bar of 9. No new source change is needed for the bar. The change is: run gates 1 to 4 and record the results. Pass means APPROVE without another code round.)

## For the two dialogue tasks

Exchange A, the one that matters: is gate 3 the minimum device evidence, or do the JVM protocol tests plus a thin adapter suffice for 9? My position: gate 3 is the minimum. The adapter is thin but it is where the only unobserved platform facts live, and a wrong `ComponentInfo.enabled` reading would disable a manifest-disabled component or skip an enabled one on every blocked start. One run, ten minutes, settles it. I will not move to 9 on reasoning alone.

Exchange B, the one I want the parent to push back on: `SettingsStoreGate.open()` and `close()` are public, and `ProcessStores.gate` is internal to the app module, so any app code can open the gate before heal. Nothing does today. Making both `internal` to settings_portability costs two keywords, needs no test, and removes the class at layer 1 of the enforcement ladder. The parent may call it hardening because no caller exists. I would accept that, but the checkpoint's question 4 should record which layer holds this class and why.

COMMENT-FIXUPS: none (review brief restricts writes to this file)

- settings_portability/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/settings_portability/SettingsStartup.kt:8-9 `open()` and `close()` can be `internal`; only `SettingsStartupCoordinator` needs them. One central change, no test needed.
- settings_rescue/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9 The comment attributes every removed permission to `:settings_android`, `notification_filter_data` and `:core`. The three new ones are merger-implied permissions from a library AAR without `targetSdkVersion`. Split the comment or name the source once the manifest-merger report shows which AAR.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/FarhanApplication.kt:32-33 CLAIM(recovery-single-process) cites a research report. Cite the observed source instead: `captures/settings/build-attempt2/evidence/app-manifest.xml:177-193` and the ACRA 5.12.0 `ACRA.kt` line.
- settings_portability/src/test/java/ly/com/tahaben/settings_portability/RecoveryComponentsTest.kt:146 `validate()` has a value case but no name case. A snapshot holding the marker name or a name without a dot is never rejected by a test. Add one line to `snapshotAndToggleFailuresRemainRecoverable`.

HARDENING-STASH:
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/ui/RescueActivity.kt:515 On API 30 and later, `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_DETAIL_SETTINGS` with `EXTRA_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_COMPONENT_NAME` opens the old Farhan's listener row directly. Polish only; the generic page works.
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/capture/CaptureEngine.kt:92 (pre-existing) `throwIfCancelled` is tested in `CaptureEngineTest` but no production caller passes it; cancel works by killing the bridge process (CLAIM(real-cancel)). Either wire a volatile flag from the cancel message or drop the parameter and its test case, so the suite does not prove a capability the product never uses.

package ly.com.tahaben.farhan.settings

import android.content.ComponentName
import android.content.Context
import android.content.ContextWrapper
import android.content.pm.ComponentInfo
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry
import ly.com.tahaben.settings_portability.*
import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Before
import org.junit.FixMethodOrder
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runners.MethodSorters
import java.io.File
import java.util.UUID

/** Run only on a disposable install. The precondition refuses existing Farhan settings before any mutation. */
@FixMethodOrder(MethodSorters.NAME_ASCENDING)
class SettingsRecoveryIntegrationTest {
    private val context get() = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().targetContext
    private val manager get() = context.packageManager
    private val marker get() = RecoveryActivity::class.java.name

    @Before fun requireDisposableInstallation() {
        assertEquals("ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha", context.packageName)
        val data = File(context.applicationInfo.dataDir)
        for (file in listOf(File(data, "shared_prefs/shared_pref.xml"),
            context.getDatabasePath("farhan_db"),
            File(context.filesDir, "datastore/farhan_data_store.preferences_pb"),
            File(context.noBackupFilesDir, "settings_import_v1"))) {
            assertFalse("Existing settings found; use a fresh disposable test install: $file", file.exists())
        }
    }

    @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
    private fun components(): List<ComponentInfo> {
        val info = manager.getPackageInfo(context.packageName, PackageManager.GET_ACTIVITIES or
            PackageManager.GET_SERVICES or PackageManager.GET_RECEIVERS or PackageManager.GET_PROVIDERS or
            PackageManager.GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS)
        return info.activities.orEmpty().toList() + info.services.orEmpty().toList() +
            info.receivers.orEmpty().toList() + info.providers.orEmpty().toList()
    }
    private fun raw(name: String) = manager.getComponentEnabledSetting(ComponentName(context.packageName, name))
    private fun set(name: String, state: Int) = manager.setComponentEnabledSetting(
        ComponentName(context.packageName, name), state, PackageManager.DONT_KILL_APP)

    // WHY: CLAIM(component-heal-exact) must hold against Android enumeration and raw overrides, not just a fake.
    // catches: omitting disabled components, treating DEFAULT as always enabled, or failing to restore raw states.
    @Test fun a_realComponentAdapterRestoresEveryNormalOverride() {
        val original = components().associate { it.name to raw(it.name) }
        val directory = File(context.cacheDir, "component-adapter-${UUID.randomUUID()}").apply { mkdirs() }
        val isolated = object : ContextWrapper(context) {
            override fun getNoBackupFilesDir(): File = directory
        }
        try {
            val enabledDefault = "ly.com.tahaben.farhan.CrashDetailsActivity"
            val explicitEnabled = SettingsBackupActivity::class.java.name
            val explicitDisabled = "ly.com.tahaben.farhan.MainActivity"
            val disabledDefault = "androidx.work.impl.background.systemalarm.ConstraintProxy\$BatteryChargingProxy"
            for (name in listOf(enabledDefault, explicitEnabled, explicitDisabled, disabledDefault))
                assertTrue("Required manifest component missing: $name", name in original)
            set(enabledDefault, PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DEFAULT)
            set(explicitEnabled, PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_ENABLED)
            set(explicitDisabled, PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED)
            set(disabledDefault, PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DEFAULT)
            val listed = components().associateBy { it.name }
            assertTrue(listed.getValue(enabledDefault).enabled)
            assertFalse(listed.getValue(disabledDefault).enabled)
            val before = listed.keys.filter { it != marker }.associateWith(::raw)

            assertTrue(RecoveryComponents(isolated).block())
            assertEquals(listed.keys, components().map { it.name }.toSet())
            assertEquals(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_ENABLED, raw(marker))
            assertEquals(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED, raw(enabledDefault))
            assertEquals(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED, raw(explicitEnabled))
            assertEquals(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED, raw(explicitDisabled))
            assertEquals(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DEFAULT, raw(disabledDefault))
            for ((name, beforeState) in before) {
                val expected = if (beforeState == PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_ENABLED ||
                    beforeState == PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DEFAULT && listed.getValue(name).enabled)
                    PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED else beforeState
                assertEquals("Blocked override for $name", expected, raw(name))
            }
            assertTrue(File(directory, "component_states_v1").exists())

            RecoveryComponents(isolated).heal()
            assertEquals(before, before.keys.associateWith(::raw))
            assertEquals(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED, raw(marker))
            assertFalse(File(directory, "component_states_v1").exists())
            assertFalse(File(directory, "component_states_v1.bak").exists())
        } finally {
            // The marker deliberately heals to DISABLED; teardown restores its original raw override too.
            original.forEach { (name, state) -> set(name, state) }
            directory.deleteRecursively()
        }
    }

    // WHY: HiltTestRunner replaces FarhanApplication, so call the actual Android startup entry explicitly.
    // catches: staging without durable replay, a gate never opened by startup, or an unwired real store adapter.
    @Test fun b_stagedImportRunsThroughAndroidStartupAndAllThreeStores() {
        try { ProcessStores.sharedPreferences(); fail("Public stores opened before startup") }
        catch (_: RecoveryRequiredException) { }
        assertTrue(SettingsStartup.run(context))
        assertEquals(StartupResult.NoImport, ProcessStores.startupResult)
        val shared = ProcessStores.sharedPreferences()
        assertTrue(shared.edit().putInt("notification_flood_threshold", 7)
            .putInt("test_internal_counter", 42)
            .putString("notification_automation_credential_v1", "destination-test-token")
            .putBoolean("notification_automation_enabled_v1", true).commit())
        val data = AndroidDataStore { ProcessStores.dataStore() }
        data.apply(emptySet(), mapOf("app_main_switch" to SettingValue.Bool(false)))
        val rows = SqlConfigurationRowsStore(AndroidSqlTransactions { ProcessStores.database().openHelper.writableDatabase })
        rows.replace(ConfigurationRows(timeLimits = listOf(TimeLimitRow("old.fixture", 1_000, 0))))
        val desired = SettingsConfiguration(
            sharedPreferences = mapOf("notification_flood_threshold" to SettingValue.Int32(17)),
            dataStore = mapOf("app_main_switch" to SettingValue.Bool(true)),
            rows = ConfigurationRows(apps = listOf(AppActivityRow("Fixture", "test.fixture", "test.fixture.Main", 0)),
                timeLimits = listOf(TimeLimitRow("test.fixture", 60_000, 0))))
        val source = PortableSource("test.fixture", "1", 1, 0)
        val preview = ImportPreview(source, 1, 1, 1, 1, emptyList())
        val bytes = PortableSettingsCodec.encode(PortableSettings(source, desired))
        assertEquals(StageResult.Staged(preview), ProcessStores.stage(bytes))
        assertEquals(ImportJournal.Staged(desired, preview), AndroidImportJournal(context.noBackupFilesDir).read())
        assertEquals(7, shared.getInt("notification_flood_threshold", -1))
        assertEquals(SettingValue.Bool(false), data.readAll()["app_main_switch"])
        assertEquals(listOf(TimeLimitRow("old.fixture", 1_000, 0)), rows.read().timeLimits)

        assertTrue(SettingsStartup.run(context))
        assertEquals(StartupResult.Applied(preview), ProcessStores.startupResult)
        assertEquals(17, ProcessStores.sharedPreferences().getInt("notification_flood_threshold", -1))
        assertEquals(42, shared.getInt("test_internal_counter", -1))
        assertFalse(shared.contains("notification_automation_credential_v1"))
        assertFalse(shared.getBoolean("notification_automation_enabled_v1", true))
        assertEquals(SettingValue.Bool(true), data.readAll()["app_main_switch"])
        assertEquals(desired.rows, rows.read())
        assertEquals(ImportJournal.Applied(preview), ProcessStores.outcome())
        ProcessStores.acknowledge()
        assertNull(ProcessStores.outcome())
        assertTrue(SettingsStartup.run(context))
        assertEquals(StartupResult.NoImport, ProcessStores.startupResult)
        assertEquals(17, shared.getInt("notification_flood_threshold", -1))
